stem: An engineer writes a unit test for `dim_customers` and saves the YAML in the project's `tests/` directory alongside the singular data tests. Running `dbt test --select "test_type:unit"` finds nothing. The definition must be discoverable without renaming the test. Where should the YAML live?

option_texts.A: In any path listed under `test-paths` in `dbt_project.yml`
option_texts.B: In `tests/generic/`, alongside the custom generic test blocks
option_texts.C: In `macros/`, because unit tests compile like macros do
option_texts.D: In a `.yml` file under `model-paths`, alongside the model

drill_answer_short: Unit tests are discovered from model-paths, not from tests/
decision_hinge: Unit tests are discovered from model-paths, by default the models directory, so define them alongside your models in a .yml file under your model-paths. Don't define unit test YAML in the tests directory, which is reserved for data tests.

plausible_options.A: The definition must be discoverable without renaming the test

B.signal: saves the YAML in the project's `tests/` directory alongside the singular data tests
B.requires_fact: Generic tests are defined in SQL files that can live in tests/generic, a special subfolder named generic within your test paths.

C.signal: An engineer writes a unit test for `dim_customers`
C.requires_fact: Generic tests work a lot like macros, and historically macros was the only place they could be defined.

distractor_traps.A: T8: scope error — test-paths governs data tests; unit tests come from model-paths
distractor_traps.B: T3: tests/generic is where custom generic data tests live, not unit tests
distractor_traps.C: T3: macros is a legitimate home for generic test blocks, but not for unit tests

stem: A team is about to refactor a complex revenue calculation. They must prove the new SQL produces the expected output for a handful of hand-written edge-case rows, and the check must run before the model is materialized anywhere. Which kind of test fits?

option_texts.A: A singular data test, which returns the rows that should not exist
option_texts.B: A unit test, which validates modelling logic against static inputs
option_texts.C: A custom generic data test, reusable across every revenue model
option_texts.D: An `accepted_values` generic test on the calculated revenue column

drill_answer_short: Unit tests validate logic on static inputs before the model is materialized
decision_hinge: Unit tests allow you to validate your SQL modeling logic on a small set of static inputs before you materialize your full model in production.

plausible_options.C: They must prove the new SQL produces the expected output for a handful of hand-written edge-case rows

A.signal: the check must run before the model is materialized anywhere
A.requires_fact: Historically, dbt's test coverage was confined to data tests, but these tests could only be executed after building a model.

D.signal: A team is about to refactor a complex revenue calculation
D.requires_fact: dbt ships with Not Null, Unique, Relationships, and Accepted Values generic data tests, which are defined as test blocks.

distractor_traps.A: T3: a singular data test is still a data test and runs only after the model is built
distractor_traps.C: T3: reusability is the wrong axis — a custom generic test is still a data test
distractor_traps.D: T8: scope error — accepted_values checks a finite value set, not a calculation's logic

stem: A custom generic test must work when applied to a source as well as to a model, so the team needs the correct standard argument name. The argument naming the resource the test is defined on is always called ____, even when the resource is a source, seed, or snapshot.
decision_hinge: The argument is always named model, even when the resource is a source, seed, or snapshot, templated out to its relation name.

stem: A test is configured with `severity: warn`, `error_if: "> 100"`, and `warn_if: "> 10"`. A run returns 250 failures. The owner must predict the status dbt reports for this test. What happens?

option_texts.A: It errors, because the failure count satisfies `error_if`
option_texts.B: It warns, because `severity: warn` skips `error_if` entirely
option_texts.C: It passes, because `warn_if` outranks the raw failure count
option_texts.D: It errors, because `severity: warn` escalates above both thresholds

drill_answer_short: With severity: warn dbt never evaluates error_if
decision_hinge: If severity is warn, dbt will skip the error_if condition entirely and jump straight to the warn_if condition. If the warn condition is met, the test warns; if it's not met, the test passes.

plausible_options.A: A test is configured with `severity: warn`, `error_if: "> 100"`, and `warn_if: "> 10"`

C.requires_fact: Conditional expressions can be any comparison logic supported by your SQL syntax with an integer number of failures.

D.signal: The owner must predict the status dbt reports for this test
D.requires_fact: By default, a test with severity warn will only ever return a warning, and not cause errors.

distractor_traps.A: T5: the error_if expression really is satisfied, but severity decides whether it is ever read
distractor_traps.C: T1: warn_if does not outrank the count — the count is what warn_if is compared against
distractor_traps.D: T1: dbt has no escalation rule that promotes a warning on volume alone

stem: One noisy test sets `store_failures: false` in its config. A scheduled job runs `dbt test --store-failures` so that every other test persists its failing rows. The team must know whether that one test writes a failures table. What happens?

option_texts.A: It writes the table, because a command-line flag wins over the config
option_texts.B: It writes the table, because the flag applies to every selected test
option_texts.C: It writes nothing, because the config takes precedence over the flag

drill_answer_short: An explicit true/false store_failures config beats the --store-failures flag
decision_hinge: If specified as true or false, the store_failures config will take precedence over the presence or absence of the --store-failures flag. If the store_failures config is none or omitted, the resource will use the value of the --store-failures flag.

plausible_options.A: A scheduled job runs `dbt test --store-failures` so that every other test persists its failing rows

B.signal: One noisy test sets `store_failures: false` in its config
B.requires_fact: The configured tests will store their failures when dbt test --store-failures is invoked.

D.signal: The team must know whether that one test writes a failures table
D.requires_fact: If you set this configuration as false but store_failures_as is configured, it will be overridden.

distractor_traps.A: T6: CLI-beats-config is the normal flag precedence rule, which store_failures deliberately inverts
distractor_traps.B: T4: it ignores the explicit per-test config named in the stem
distractor_traps.D: T1: --store-failures has no dependency on store_failures_as being set

stem: A production job runs `dbt build` nightly and the team must cut its compute cost without losing any coverage that production actually needs. The project has a large suite of unit tests whose inputs are fixed fixtures. What is the BEST change, given data tests must keep running nightly?

option_texts.A: Replace the production `dbt build` with `dbt run`, then `dbt test` later
option_texts.B: Set every unit test to `severity: warn` so failures stop blocking the job
option_texts.C: Exclude unit tests from the production build using a resource-type flag
option_texts.D: Move the unit tests into `tests/` so the nightly build stops discovering them

drill_answer_short: Static inputs mean unit tests earn nothing in production — exclude them by resource type
decision_hinge: dbt Labs strongly recommends only running unit tests in development or CI environments. Since the inputs of the unit tests are static, there's no need to use additional compute cycles running them in production. Use the resource type flag --exclude-resource-type to exclude unit tests from your production builds and save compute.

plausible_options.A: the team must cut its compute cost without losing any coverage that production actually needs
plausible_options.D: The project has a large suite of unit tests whose inputs are fixed fixtures

B.signal: data tests must keep running nightly
B.requires_fact: By default, a test with severity warn will only ever return a warning, and not cause errors.

distractor_traps.A: T7: splitting the schedule loses dbt build's DAG-order skipping and still runs the unit tests
distractor_traps.B: T2: severity changes what a failure means, not whether the test consumes compute
distractor_traps.D: T3: tests/ is reserved for data tests, so this hides the unit tests rather than scheduling them properly

stem: A team must understand what `dbt build` does to a single SQL model that has both unit tests and data tests defined. Put the steps in the order dbt performs them for that model.
build_items: Run the unit tests on the model
Materialize the model in the warehouse
Run the data tests on the model
Run the data tests on the model's parents
drill_answer: Run the unit tests on the model
Materialize the model in the warehouse
Run the data tests on the model
drill_answer_short: Unit tests, then materialize, then data tests
decision_hinge: Use dbt build to, in lineage order, run the unit tests on your model, materialize your model in the warehouse, and run the data tests on your model.

stem: A project on dbt v1.10.5 or higher must write an `accepted_values` test so that its `values` list is passed correctly. Any arguments or configurations passed to a generic data test should be nested below the ____ property.
decision_hinge: Any arguments or configurations passed to those data tests should be nested below the arguments property.
